title: Dottie and Whisper's Star Picnic
markdown:
Dottie was not a boo kind of witch. She was a let’s-make-everything-extra-cozy-and-sparkly kind. Her hat was deep dreamy purple, the colour of a sky tucking itself in. Her broom did not whoosh like a grumpy gust; it hummed like a happy bumblebee. Whisper, her snow-white mouse, had whiskers that wiggled with curiosity and fur like a fresh snowball.

Their cottage sat at the edge of the Wobblecap Mountains, which were not wobbly, only bumpy, like giants who had forgotten to smooth their beds. It smelled of cinnamon cookies and warm blankets. Tonight the sky was velvety blue, sprinkled with a gazillion tiny diamonds winking like night lights.

“Whisper,” Dottie said, eyes like shiny blueberries, “it’s a perfect night for a picnic. A star-picnic.”

Whisper stopped mid-groom on the sunny windowsill. He squeaked, nose wiggling, always ready if even the tiniest crumb of cheese might be involved.

She packed a basket the right size for a witch and a mouse: a blanket soft as a scrap of sky, star-shaped sandwiches of moonbeam cheese that glowed a little, a thermos of warm bubbly cocoa. “Ready, my little fluffernutter?” Whisper perched on her shoulder, puffed his chest, and nodded.

They set off toward the Tinkling Fir Grove. The mountains humped along beside them, rumpled and friendly. When wind moved the needles, the trees made an orchestra of tiny fairy bells. Tinkle-tinkle-tinkle. Dottie hummed along. Whisper’s ears perked for every note, claws hardly a sound on the purple hat’s brim.

Deeper in, moonlight filtered through the branches, a silvery glow painting dancing patterns on the floor. A rustle, then another, then another, like a very happy hedgehog doing a contented sigh. They peeked around a giant mossy tree whose bark felt rough and cool as ancient velvet. A muffled puff of air escaped, smelling of earth and sweet dreams. Snuffle-snuffle. Fast asleep: a wizard apprentice, pointy hat tilted over his eyes like a sleepy sombrero, snoring the softest gentlest snores, holding a small bunch of flowers that looked like tiny curled-up yawns. Pale soft blue. Faint shimmer. Flicker, known for taking little afternoon naps.

Dottie plucked one dreamy flower and tucked it into Whisper’s pocket. He sniffed; his eyes fluttered; he sighed honey and quiet dreams. “We’ll leave you to your nap, Flicker.” They went on, the flower adding a peaceful thread to the path.

The clearing they found was moonlight on springy moss that yielded like a velvet cushion. Dottie spread the tiny blanket. Whisper, with great importance, helped arrange the star-shaped sandwiches. Plink: a particularly bright star winked, as if saying hello. Dottie looked up at the inky-blue sky, heart full and warm as cocoa. Whisper snuggled into her lap, tiny paws on the cloth. The night itself felt like a giant friendly blanket full of sparkling friends. She sat back, breathed night flowers and earth, and let the thousand tiny bright eyes watch. For a moment there was only the gentle hum of night, the distant tinkle of the firs, and the quiet joy of being together. Peaceful. Content. No need to call it the best part. It simply was.

After nibbling, moonbeam cheese a delightful surprise, Dottie said, “It’s getting a little cooler now, isn’t it, Whisper?” A tiny nod, whiskers brushing her chin like a tickle. “Time for our cocoa.” She poured the warm bubbly drink into two tiny acorn cups, perfectly sweet, warming them from noses to toes.

A soft hee-hee-hee. Flicker had woken, yawned a giant yawn, and followed the grove’s tinkling to their spot, shy, eyes like little stars.

“I saw your picnic. May I join?”

“Of course. Come sit.”

Flicker sat on the moss. They shared the rest of the star-shaped sandwiches. He told a funny story about accidentally turning his spellbook into a fluffy kitten. Dottie shared the time her extra-crispy toast spell made the bread sing opera, very loudly. Whisper listened, nibbled a crumb, and squeaked agreement that sounded like tiny enthusiastic applause. A witch, a mouse, and a sleepy apprentice did not need a speech about difference. They all loved the quiet magic of the night.

Soon the stars began to fade and the sky turned a soft dusky pink, like a strawberry smoothie. “Time to head home,” Dottie said, stretching. Flicker nodded, sleepiness almost gone, replaced by a warm glow. “I’ll walk with you.”

So they went back through the now-waking fir grove. Tinkling softer, sleepy whispers of wind. Dottie held Whisper close, white fur a comfort against her cheek. Flicker hummed a quiet happy tune. They talked about the stars, the kitten spellbook, how yummy moonbeam cheese is, and how even sleepy apprentices can find a picnic.

Back at the cottage Dottie poured Flicker a mug of extra-warm extra-cocoa-y cocoa, the kind that makes you toasty inside. He thanked her with a smile that spread all across his face, waved, promised to visit again soon, and headed toward his own cozy nook.

Dottie carried a very sleepy Whisper to bed. The dreamy flower in the pocket released a faint sweet scent, a lullaby sung just for them. Covers high. Whisper tucked safely beside her, one last contented sigh. They closed their eyes and drifted, dreaming of tinkling trees, friendly stars, and the picnic that had made room for a third cup.
